subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make only the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: Current code, tests, and release behavior encode read-only `none`, but maintainer discussion rejects strict write-tool hiding and says the intended permanent fix is isolated-writable `none`; this is a sandbox boundary decision, not a safe automated cleanup.

options.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require a full mount, bridge, tool, docs, and live-proof update.

options.title: Keep None Read-Only
options.body: Retain the current fail-closed behavior and update docs/support guidance so file-producing workflows use `rw` or a future explicit writable mode.

options.title: Resolve With Custom-Bind Policy
options.body: Handle this together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718 if maintainers want one broader least-privilege write model.

recommendation.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require a full mount, bridge, tool, docs, and live-proof update.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer direction on the adjacent PR explicitly keeps this issue as the canonical sandbox contract decision.
